items.excerpt: ## Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervenes Nov 24, 2026 Jensen Huang is back as CEO of the chip giant Nvidia, after President Trump personally called into a meeting of the company’s board on Sunday to push for his reinstatement. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago, after news reports revealed he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly in communication with China’s top spy agency. The woman worked with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of buying advanced Nvidia chips and then diverting them to China in violation of U.S. export rules. On Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist. During an interview on CNBC, President Trump was questioned about his role in reinstating Huang. > Eamon Javers: “Mr. President, did you give the board of directors an assurance that Jensen Huang would not be prosecuted at all for any of these” — > President Donald Trump: “I didn’t use the word 'prosecuted.'”

items.title: Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist
items.excerpt: Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool. The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2. Confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board said, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. Still, confidence among Republicans remained the highest among the three groups. While respondents "continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs," they also "cited hope for the general economy," said Fergus McCormick, the board's senior economist for global indicators. The survey comes with the Federal Reserve continuing to try to bring down inflation, which has run above the central bank's 2% target for some 5½ years. The Fed is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point when it meets again in two weeks. Despite the lingering worries about the cost of living — a centerpiece issue during the midterms — the survey's present situation and expectations indexes both posted strong gains. Inflation expectations for 12 months from now fell for the second straight month but remained high at 5.7%. The survey's closely watched gap between jobs considered "plentiful" versus "hard to get" widened to 12.4 percentage points. The "plentiful" side rose to 30.8% from 26.2% while "hard to get" fell to 18.4%, down 3 percentage points.

items.title: November 24 | Federal Reserve: Williams Expects US Headline PCE Inflation of About 3.5% This Year · Goodman Macro
items.excerpt: On November 23, 2026, at 4 p.m. Eastern Time, Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams delivered a speech at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in the Bronx, New York. In his assessment, the US labor market is broadly in balance, risks to maximum employment have eased, and risks to price stability are rising. Previously, on October 28, the Federal Reserve voted 10 to 2 to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4%; the two dissenting officials favored a 25-basis-point increase. In considering whether the next move should be a rate increase, Williams is watching whether pressure from higher energy and chip prices spreads beyond a small group of goods to a broader range of business and household spending. He noted that elevated prices for energy and artificial intelligence-related goods are expected to push US headline personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation to about 3.5% in 2026. ... On the goods side, Williams said that the upward effect of import tariffs on goods prices has diminished substantially; current price pressures mainly stem from energy and AI-related demand. The conflict in the Middle East and constrained refining capacity have lifted crude oil prices, while the spreads between gasoline and diesel prices and crude oil have also widened. This makes the cost of refined fuels purchased by businesses less likely to fall than crude oil prices. Meanwhile, data center construction is driving chip purchases, with supply struggling to keep pace with demand in the short term. If AI investment accelerates further, the prices of related products will remain under upward pressure. Inflation pressures from services and wages are relatively contained. Price increases for housing-related services have slowed. Williams said there is little evidence in the available data that wage growth is adding to inflation, and medium- to longer-term inflation expectations in surveys and financial markets remain stable. He expects US headline PCE inflation to be about 3.5% in 2026. Provided that energy prices normalize and supply and demand for AI-related goods gradually come into balance, he expects headline PCE inflation to fall to slightly above 2% in 2027 and return to 2% in 2028. This path represents Williams's assessment of the inflation outlook; he did not signal a rate decision for the next meeting in his speech. ... The flash November S&P Global US Composite Output Index, released that morning, fell to 54.6 from October's final reading of 55.9. Manufacturing and services remained in expansion overall, but growth slowed to its weakest pace since July. Increases in both input costs and selling prices eased among the businesses surveyed. Manufacturers nevertheless continued to face substantial cost pressure, and shortages of some metals and electronic components lengthened delivery times. items.title: Preview: Due November 25 - U.S. October Personal Income and
items.excerpt: # Preview: Due November 25 - U.S. October Personal Income and Spending - 5-month high for yr/yr core PCE prices We expect October to see gains of 0.4% in personal income and personal spending, while PCE prices rise by 0.3% both overall and ex food and energy, meaning only marginal gains for income and spending in real terms. We expect the core PCE price index to be close to 0.3% even before rounding, as was the core CPI. Overall CPI rose by close to 0.35% before rounding. With PCE prices generally less sensitive to gasoline than CPI we expect overall PCE prices will round down to 0.3% rather than rounding up to 0.4%, as was the case for the CPI. This is likely to mean accelerations in yr/yr growth, overall PCE prices to 3.8% from 3.6% and the core rate to 3.2% from 3.1%. These would both be the highest since matching gains in May. A strong October non-farm payroll breakdown, in employment, the workweek and average hourly earnings, implies a healthy 0.5% rise in wages and salaries. Overall personal income is however likely to be slightly slower than this, at 0.4%. Retail sales increased by 0.2% in October restrained by weakness in autos. We expect services to rise by 0.5%, in line with September’s gain, leaving overall spending matching incomes 0.4% increase.

items.title: Shutdown odds rise as Democrats seek fragile Iran deal
items.excerpt: Senate negotiators are trying to thread the needle and find a deal to avoid a government shutdown before Christmas, but progress has been slowed by a Senate Democratic leadership fight. The key issue is the Iran war, which was a major factor in the sweeping Democratic midterm election victories. Senate negotiators are sketching the outlines of a deal that would provide the Trump administration with critical funding to replenish weapons and munitions stockpiles that have been depleted by the Iran war, but that would purport to stop funding the conflict itself. The question is whether that deal can be accepted by progressive Democrats who have called for an immediate end to the war, or by President Trump, as his administration would get far less money than it sought. And then there’s the complication of the Senate leadership fight pitting progressive Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) against Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (N.Y.). That battle is putting pressure on Schumer to keep his distance from the funding talks, since it could cost him support within his own conference. Senators in both parties say they desperately want to avoid another shutdown, but party strategists say the odds of one increase each day Congress lurches closer to the Dec. 11 deadline. ... Democrats say that any funding to maintain the naval blockade of Iranian ports or to conduct other activities that could be defined as “acts of war” toward Iran cannot come out of new money appropriated in a December funding deal.
